title.narrative: Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia (Ktk)
Stärka kvinnors rättigheter och kvinnors deltagande i Nordmakedonien (Ktk)

description.narrative:
Kvinna till Kvinna har ansökt om finansiering på 18 500 000 SEK för att genomföra projektet "Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia" under perioden 2020-2023.
Det övergripande målet för projektet är att Kvinna till Kvinna och dess lokala partnerorganisationer ska påverka politik och praxis när det gäller könsbaserat våld, agendan för kvinnor, fred och säkerhet (WPS-agendan) och kvinnors ekonomiska befogenheter i Nordmakedonien.
Projektet presenterar fyra delmål - ett för vart och ett av de tre tematiska områdena och ett fjärde som täcker alla områden:
1. Partnerorganisationer bidrar till bättre tillgång till rättslig prövning för rättighetsbärare och rättsstatsprinciper genom policy- och attitydförändringar avseende genusbaserat våld. 2. Partnerorganisationer skapar förutsättningar för kvinnor och flickor att delta fullt och effektivt i utvecklingen av ett jämlikt och demokratiskt samhälle och för genomförandet av agendan för kvinnor, fred och säkerhet (WPS-agendan). 3. Organisationer som nås inom projektet bidrar till förändringar i politik och praxis när det gäller kvinnors ekonomiska bemyndigande. 4. Ett mer levande civilsamhälle genom ökad hållbarhet för organisationer som fokuserar på kvinnors rättigheter.
Projektet kommer att genomföras av Kvinna till Kvinna i samarbete med relevanta partnerorganisationer.
Sida är den enda givaren som har blivit tillfrågad om att ge stöd till denna insats.

Kvinna till kvinna has applied to the Embassy of Sweden for funding of 18,5 MSEK to carry out the project "Strenghtening womens rights and womens participation in North Macedonia" during the period 2020-2023.
The overall objective of the project is that Kvinna till Kvinna and partner organisations will influence policy and practice regarding gender-based violence, the women peace and security agenda and women’s economic empowerment in North Macedonia.
The project presents four intermediate objectives - one for each of the three thematic areas and a fourth covering all areas:
1. Partner organisations contribute to better access to justice for rights holders and rule of law through policy and attitude changes regarding GBV. 2. Partner organisations create conditions for women and girls to participate fully and effectively in the development of an equal and democratic society, and towards the implementation of the women, peace and security agenda. 3. Organisations reached within the program contribute to changes in policy and practice regarding women’s economic empowerment. 4. A more vibrant civil society through increased sustainability of women’s rights organisations.
The project will be implemented by Kvinna till Kvinna in collaboration with relevant partner organisations.
Sida is the only donor invited by Kvinna till kvinna for support of this intervention.

The overall objective of the project is that Kvinna till Kvinna and local partner organisations will influence policy and practice regarding gender-based violence, the women peace and security agenda and women’s economic empowerment in North Macedonia. By working towards this objective, the project aims to contribute to the long-term outcome which states: North Macedonia is a democratic society where women’s rights and participation is secured, with a vibrant and pluralistic civil society. Moreover, the project presents four intermediate objectives - one for each of the three thematic areas and a fourth covering all areas. 1. Partner organisations contribute to better access to justice for rights holders and rule of law through policy and attitude changes regarding GBV. 2. Partner organisations create conditions for women and girls to participate fully and effectively in the development of an equal and democratic society, and towards the implementation of the women, peace and security agenda. 3. Organisations reached within the program contribute to changes in policy and practice regarding women’s economic empowerment. 4. A more vibrant civil society through increased sustainability of women’s rights organisations. Each of the above intermediate objectives have corresponding outputs that will be monitored throughout the project. Through the support to and cooperation with partner organisations, Kvinna till Kvinna will use advocacy to influence relevant stakeholders at local, national and international level. Apart from advocacy, the main methods that Kvinna till Kvinna will use to reach the programme goals are financial and political support to women’s rights organisations, capacity development, networking, communication and outreach. The target groups of the intervention are manifold - both at local and national levels as well as targeting the public. For instance, the project aims to have an influence on local municipalities, mayors and civil society organisations, as well as national government, ministries and intersectoral working groups.

description.narrative:
Even though this is a new contribution implemented by Ktk, which is supported through the bilateral support, this project is building on earlier experiences, established networks and vast knowledge of Ktk in the area collected in more than 20 years of experience and work in the country.
Benefiting from above, during the implementing period this project has achieved good results and stimulated positive processes continuing Ktk's work in organizing the country's Women Civil Society Sector (WCSS), supporting strengthened watch-dog role of the contracted POs, and providing support to intensify and increase number of activities implemented by WCSOs both in the urban and rural areas in the country.
Outreach and mobilization of young women is an important focus.
Also, a great attention is placed on countering the spreading of the global anti-gender movements into the country , which is an increasing threat to democracy and human rights .
Seven different Partner organizations signed an Agreement with Kvinna till kvinna for cooperation and implementation of one, two- or three-year projects . However, one contracted partner organization was phased out in agreement with Sida.
Two of the Partner Organizations were authorized to provide subgrating to 11 third party organizations which are mainly active in the rural areas and small urban communities.
The supported third-party organizations include: National Roma Center from the city of (c.) Kumanovo; Vizija, c. Kavadarci; Organisation of Women, c. Veles; Semper, c. Bitola; Cortex, c.Tetovo; Civic Initiative of Women, c. Sveti Nikole; Majka, c. Kumanovo; Organisation of Women, c. Strumica; Radika De, c. Debar; Womens Action, c. Radovis; Womens Lobby, c. Demir Kapija.
The EU-integration process is used as a leverage toward key stakeholders in the programme. Kvinna till kvinna in its overall position as a responsible project implementing partner and process initiator, directly contributed to this process , and achieved the following main results:
- Facilitating ad-hoc dialogue between Delegation of the European Union (EUD) and POs, while aiming to establish this dialogue on regular bases.
- Supporting the EUD in developing a Country-Level Implementation Plan for North Macedonia (CLIP) in line with the EU gender Action Plan (GAP) III, by providing inputs generated through a process in which the Gender Equality Platform, Reactor and other KtK's PO were involved.
-Strengthening of international advocacy in synergy with Kvinna till Kvinnas EU Advocacy program where the National Network and HERA - Association for health, education and research - hera.org.mk provided input to the European Commission Country Report for North Macedonia.
- Providing an introductory information on preparation of new draft documents relevant to gender equality area, including: the Law on Gender Equality, the National Gender Equality Strategy 2021-2026, the Law against Discrimination at Work, and the Law on Labor Relations, a new Roma inclusion Strategy 2022-2030 and a National Action Plan (NAP) for Roma women .
The results achieved by contracted six POs under the program include:
- Successfully implemented protest in February 2021 by the Gender equality platform in response to the online sexual harassment of women and girls in the Public room scandal. Some 500 Women Human Right Defenders demonstrated and shared their concerns about the impunity, while urging authorities to ensure protection and to introduce and implement specific legislation on Gender Based Violence (GBV) online. - Supported local WCSOs monitored the implementation of national legal frameworks on the local level, and advocated for allocation of municipal funds for subsidies and financial assistance to survivors of GBV and Domestic Violence (DV) ; - Capacity is built of future practitioners dealing with DV cases (17 young lawyers) in understanding of DV overall, and the specific legal needs of women survivors of GBV. - Legal empowerment of women GBV survivors by providing free legal assistance (168 women supported during 2021), and in court representation, as well as providing psychological support. - Implementation of a comprehensive awareness raising campaign throughout the year, informing about how to recognize DV, including specific forms of psychological and sexual violence. The awareness campaign incorporated 77 social media posts and messages, production of four documentary videos, three video testimonials with women survivors, press releases, participation on national TV. Also, information was shared on the legal and psychological services provided through established Legal Aid Centre and online platform pobarajsovet.mk. The reported reach of this campaign is 411.085, including 197.166 persons reached within the international awareness raising campaign "16 Days of Activism Against Gender Based Violence. - Established informal network of women activists and organizations named "Women's Circle" as a growing platform for mutual support and exchange of experiences among the grassroot organizations and newly emerging women activists. An established network of supported 11 WCSO's works in 21 municipalities and 60 villages/urban communities, covering 1/4 of the country. - The marginalized group of Roma women were supported by the National Roma Center c. Kumanovo focusing on facilitating of employment by contributing to development of a favorable political climate as well as to the process of development of the National Action Plan for Roma women and a new Roma Inclusion Strategy;
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
